spots.name: Salt Lake Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Salt Lake Temple is a temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on Temple Square in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. Dedicated in 1893, it was constructed over a period of 40 years.

spots.name: Salt Lake Tabernacle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Salt Lake Tabernacle, formerly known as the Mormon Tabernacle, is located on Temple Square in Salt Lake City, in the U.S. state of Utah. The tabernacle was built from 1863 to 1875 to house meetings for the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

names.ja: ソルトレイク・タバナクル

spots.name: Cathedral of the Madeleine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of the Madeleine is a Catholic cathedral in Salt Lake City, Utah, in the United States. It was completed in 1909 and is the cathedral, or mother church, of the Diocese of Salt Lake City.

names.fr: Cathédrale Sainte-Madeleine de Salt Lake City
names.es: Catedral de la Magdalena de Salt Lake City

spots.name: Temple Square
spots.summary: Temple Square is a 10-acre (4.0 ha) complex, owned by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, in the center of Salt Lake City, Utah. The usage of the name has gradually changed to include several other church facilities that are immediately adjacent to Temple Square.

names.it: Piazza del Tempio di Salt Lake City

spots.name: Utah State Capitol

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Utah State Capitol is the house of government for the U.S. state of Utah. The building houses the chambers and offices of the Utah State Legislature, the offices of the governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general, the state auditor and their staffs.

spots.name: Church Office Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church Office Building is a 28-story building in Salt Lake City, Utah, which houses the administrative support staff for the lay ministry of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints throughout the world.

spots.name: Fort Douglas
spots.summary: Fort Douglas was established in October 1862, during the American Civil War, as a small military garrison about three miles east of Salt Lake City, Utah. Its purpose was to protect the overland mail route and telegraph lines along the Central Overland Route.

spots.name: Seagull Monument
spots.summary: The Seagull Monument is a historic monument situated immediately east of the Salt Lake Assembly Hall on Temple Square, in Salt Lake City, Utah.

photo.author: Ben P L from Provo, USA

spots.name: Salt Lake Assembly Hall

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Salt Lake Assembly Hall is a building owned by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints which sits on the southwest corner of Temple Square in Salt Lake City, Utah. It has seating capacity for an audience of approximately 1,400 people.

spots.name: Joseph Smith Memorial Building
spots.summary: The Joseph Smith Memorial Building (JSMB), originally called the Hotel Utah, is a social center located on the corner of Main Street and South Temple in Salt Lake City. It is named in honor of Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement.

spots.name: Astra Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Astra Tower, known during construction as Kensington Tower, is a high-rise residential skyscraper in Downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. Rising to 41 stories and 449 feet (137 m) in height, it is the tallest building in both the city and state.

spots.name: Brigham Young Monument
spots.summary: The Brigham Young Monument is a bronzed historical monument located on the north sidewalk of the intersection at Main and South Temple Streets of Salt Lake City, Utah.

photo.author: Artist: Cyrus Edwin Dallin (November 22, 1861 – November 14, 1944) Photo: Dundak

spots.name: City Creek Center
spots.summary: City Creek Center (CCC), commonly shortened to City Creek, is a mixed-use development containing an upscale open-air shopping mall, grocery store, and office and residential buildings near Temple Square in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States.

spots.name: Salt Lake City and County Building

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Salt Lake City and County Building, usually called the "City-County Building", is the seat of government for Salt Lake City, Utah. The historic landmark formerly housed offices for Salt Lake County government as well, hence the name.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Salt Lake City and County Building

spots.name: Endowment House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Endowment House was an early building used by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints to administer temple ordinances in Salt Lake City, Utah Territory.

spots.name: Liberty Park
spots.summary: Liberty Park is a popular public urban park in Salt Lake City, Utah. It is the city's second-largest public park, at 80 acres (32 ha), being surpassed only by Sugar House Park which has 110.5 acres (44.7 ha). The park features a pond with two islands, and is also the location of Tracy Aviary.

spots.name: Church History Museum
spots.summary: The Church History Museum, formerly the Museum of Church History and Art, is the premier museum operated by the Church History Department of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. It is located in Salt Lake City, Utah, and is opposite the west gates of the church's Temple Square.

spots.name: FamilySearch Library

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The FamilySearch Library (FSL), formerly the Family History Library, is a genealogical research facility in downtown Salt Lake City. The library is open to the public free of charge and is operated by FamilySearch, the genealogical arm of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

spots.name: Gallivan Center
spots.summary: The John W. Gallivan Utah Center, is an urban plaza in the heart of Downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States.

photo.author: Ben P L from Provo, USA

spots.name: Eagle Gate
spots.summary: The Eagle Gate is a historical monument which forms an arch across State Street in the downtown area of Salt Lake City, Utah. The monument pays homage to Brigham Young's 1859 Eagle Gate, which served as an entrance to his property and the City Creek Canyon road.

spots.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Holy Trinity Cathedral, also known as Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Church, is a Greek Orthodox cathedral in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. Built in 1923, the church was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1975.

names.fr: Cathédrale de la Sainte-Trinité de Salt Lake City

spots.name: Natural History Museum of Utah
spots.summary: The Natural History Museum of Utah is a museum located in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. The museum shows exhibits of natural history subjects, with an emphasis on Utah and the Intermountain West. The mission of the museum is to illuminate the natural world and the place of humans within it.

spots.name: Eccles Theater
spots.summary: The George S. and Dolores Doré Eccles Theater is located in Salt Lake City, Utah. Opened in 2016, it hosts touring Broadway shows, concerts, and other entertainment events. The primary "Delta Performance Hall" seats 2,468 people, while a smaller black box theater seats 150-250 people.

spots.name: St. Mark's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of Saint Mark, commonly known as St. Mark's Cathedral, is the cathedral church of the Episcopal Diocese of Utah. It is located on 100 South in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah.

spots.name: Salt Lake City Public Library
spots.summary: The Salt Lake City Public Library system's main branch building is an architecturally unique structure in Salt Lake City, Utah. It is located at 210 East 400 South, across from the Salt Lake City and County Building and Washington Square.

names.es: Biblioteca pública de Salt Lake City
names.ja: ソルト・レイク・シティ公共図書館

spots.name: Brigham Young Complex
spots.summary: The Brigham Young Complex is a collection of buildings historically associated with the second President and leader of the LDS Church Brigham Young, on East South Temple in the center of Salt Lake City, Utah.

photo.author: Original uploader was SLCMormon at en.wikipedia

spots.name: Sugar House Monument
spots.summary: Erected in 1930, the Sugar House Monument has long stood as a testament to the hard work of early Salt Lake pioneers making the valley sustainable.

photo.author: The original uploader was JonMoore at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Walker Center
spots.summary: Walker Center is a skyscraper in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States.

spots.name: Rice–Eccles Stadium
spots.summary: Rice–Eccles Stadium is an outdoor college football stadium located on the campus of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, Utah. It is the home field of the Utah Utes of the Big 12 Conference.

names.ja: ライス・エクルズ・スタジアム

spots.name: Restoration of the Melchizedek Priesthood
spots.summary: Restoration of the Melchizedek Priesthood is a 1960s bronze sculpture by Avard Fairbanks. The artwork was commissioned by the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints for Temple Square in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States.

spots.name: Olympic and Paralympic Cauldron Plaza
spots.summary: The Olympic and Paralympic Cauldron Plaza is located outside the southwestern corner of Rice–Eccles Stadium on the campus of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, Utah. During the 2002 Winter Olympics and Paralympics, the stadium was known as Rice-Eccles Olympic Stadium and hosted the Opening and Closing Ceremonies.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Olympic and Paralympic Cauldron Plaza (Salt Lake City)

spots.name: The Leonardo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Leonardo, located in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States was a science and art museum where visitors could explore the ways that science, technology, art, and creativity connect. The museum operated from 2011 to 2025.

spots.name: Restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood
spots.summary: Restoration of the Aaronic Priesthood: John the Baptist is a 1957 bronze sculpture by Avard Fairbanks, installed in Salt Lake City’s Temple Square, in the U.S. state of Utah.

spots.name: Salt Lake City Council Hall
spots.summary: The Salt Lake City Council Hall is a historic building located on Capitol Hill in Salt Lake City, Utah. Built from 1864 to 1866, it was used as the city hall for Salt Lake City from 1866 to 1894.

spots.name: ZCMI Cast Iron Front
spots.summary: The ZCMI Cast Iron Front is a historic building façade, currently attached to City Creek Center facing Main Street in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States.

spots.name: Beehive sculptures
spots.summary: Two sculptures of beehives are installed outside the Utah State Capitol in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. The artworks were presented to the state by the Kennecott Copper Corporation on July 24, 1976. They are located on the grand staircase on the south side of the Capitol.

spots.name: First Presbyterian Church of Salt Lake City

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The First Presbyterian Church of Salt Lake City is a Presbyterian Church congregation in Salt Lake City, Utah. It was founded in 1871. From 1874-1905 the church met in a building at the corner of Second South and Second East, which has since been demolished.
spots.wikipediaTitle: First Presbyterian Church of Salt Lake City

spots.name: Museum of Utah

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Utah is the state history museum of Utah. Operated by the Utah State Historical Society, it also houses the state's history research center and is located at the Utah State Capitol complex in Salt Lake City, Utah. The museum opened in June 2026, becoming the state's first official history museum.

spots.name: Mormon Battalion Monument
spots.summary: The Mormon Battalion Monument is installed outside the Utah State Capitol in Salt Lake City, in the U.S. state of Utah.

spots.name: White Community Memorial Chapel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: White Community Memorial Chapel is a historic, non-denominational meetinghouse on Capitol Hill in Salt Lake City, Utah. The structure was built from 1979 to 1980 with salvaged elements from the recently demolished Salt Lake 18th Ward meetinghouse, which had been constructed in the early 1880s.

spots.name: Independent Order of Odd Fellows Hall
spots.summary: The Independent Order of Odd Fellows Hall, also known as the I.O.O.F. Hall, is a historic clubhouse in Downtown, Salt Lake City, Utah, United States, that is listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP).
spots.wikipediaTitle: Independent Order of Odd Fellows Hall (Salt Lake City)

spots.name: Washington Square
spots.summary: Washington Square, or Washington Square Park, is a public park in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. The park surrounds the Salt Lake City and County Building, which houses Salt Lake City's government.

spots.name: Old Hansen Planetarium
spots.summary: The Old Hansen Planetarium is a three-story building located at 15 South State Street in Salt Lake City, Utah. It has served many functions throughout its history. Originally built in 1904 as the Salt Lake City Public Library, the building was renovated in 1965 to become the Hansen Planetarium.

spots.name: Main Street
spots.summary: Main Street is the most important commercial street in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States, though it also extends south into the cities of South Salt Lake, Millcreek, and Murray.

spots.name: Utah Museum of Contemporary Art

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: The Utah Museum of Contemporary Art (UMOCA), formerly known as the Salt Lake Art Center, is a contemporary art museum located in downtown Salt Lake City. The museum presents rotating exhibitions by local, national, and international contemporary artists throughout its six gallery spaces.

spots.name: First National Bank
spots.summary: The First National Bank is a historic bank building in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States, that is listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP).

spots.name: First Security Bank Building
spots.summary: The First Security Bank Building in Salt Lake City, Utah, is a 12-story International Style commercial structure built in 1954. The building was designed by Wenceslao Sarmiento in consultation with W.G.

spots.name: Peery Hotel
spots.summary: The Peery Hotel in Salt Lake City, Utah, is a 3-story Prairie style building that incorporates Classical Revival design elements. The hotel was designed by Charles B. Onderdonk and Irving Goodfellow and constructed in 1910 in what is now the city's Warehouse District.

spots.name: Japanese Church of Christ

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Japanese Church of Christ is a historic church at 268 W. 100 South in Salt Lake City, Utah.

spots.name: Brigham Young Historic Park
spots.summary: Brigham Young Historic Park is a park near Temple Square in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. Built in 1995, along with its companion park, City Creek Park, it was created to provide additional urban green space in the downtown area.

spots.name: Church History Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church History Library (CHL) is a research center and archives building housing materials chronicling the history of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. The library is owned by the Church and opened in 2009 in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah.

spots.name: Exchange Place Historic District
spots.summary: The Exchange Place Historic District in Downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States is a historic district that was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978. It included ten contributing buildings and three non-contributing buildings on a 6.2-acre (2.5 ha) area, with significance dating to 1903.

spots.name: Pioneer Memorial Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Pioneer Memorial Museum is a history museum operated by the Daughters of Utah Pioneers (DUP) on Capitol Hill in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. The museum hosts a large collection of artifacts related to the Mormon pioneers and early Utah, along with libraries containing pioneer biographies and photographs.

spots.name: Belvedere Apartments
spots.summary: The Belvedere Apartments is a historic residential building in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah. Opened as an "apartment hotel" in 1919, the structure was constructed by the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and leased to James T. Keith to operate.

spots.name: Bust of Charles Roscoe Savage
spots.summary: A 1928 bust of Charles Roscoe Savage by Gilbert Riswold is installed in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States.

spots.name: Social Hall

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Social Hall was a historic theater and multi-use building in Salt Lake City, Utah.

spots.name: McIntyre Building
spots.summary: The McIntyre Building is a historic commercial building in downtown Salt Lake City, Utah, United States, that is listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRHP).

spots.name: McCornick Building
spots.summary: The McCornick Building, at 10 W. 100 South in Salt Lake City, Utah, was built in 1890–93. It is also known as the Crandall Building. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1977.

spots.name: New York Hotel
spots.summary: The New York Hotel in Salt Lake City, Utah, at 42 Post Office Pl., was built in 1906. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980.

spots.name: University of Utah Circle
spots.summary: The University of Utah Circle, also known as Presidents Circle, is located on the campus of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City, Utah, United States. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978 as a historic district.

photo.author: Scott Catron from Sandy, Utah, USA

spots.name: Jon M. Huntsman Center
spots.summary: The university's main indoor venue, home to men's and women's basketball, women's volleyball, and women's gymnastics. Basketball history buffs may recognize it as the site of the 1979 NCAA men's basketball Final Four; the championship game was the first meeting between all-time greats Larry Bird and Magic Johnson (Magic was on the winning side that time).

names.ja: ジョン・M・ハンツマンセンター

spots.name: Salt Lake City Main Library
spots.summary: One of Salt Lake City's most unique pieces of architecture, the library makes use of natural light and features a rooftop garden. The Rooftop Terrace is closed for renovations as of December 2024.

spots.name: The Red Iguana
spots.summary: Mexican restaurant with a menu based on old family recipes. Popular and crowded enough that they have a second location less than two blocks away (866 W South Temple, ) and an express version called Taste of Red Iguana a mile (2 km) east on the State Street side of the City Creek Center mall.

spots.name: The Pie Pizzeria

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Two locations around the corner from each other: one for take-out only and then a dine-in location in a dark but cozy basement with twenty years worth of graffiti covering the walls. Best known for their giant, thickly loaded pizzas, but they also serve salads, sub sandwiches, and beer.

spots.name: The Bayou

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: A beer lover's paradise with over 300 different beers from all over the world, about 30 of them on tap. The food menu features Cajun and Creole dishes like Jambalaya Pizza, Alligator Cheesecake, and Blackened Catfish Salad. Live music after 9PM on most Friday and Saturday nights.

spots.name: Brewvies

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cinema pub with two movie screens and a lineup of mostly recent releases. Menu consists of things like pizza, burgers, nachos, and chicken tenders; drinks are mostly beer, including many local brews. Food bought at Brewvies can be eaten in the theater areas.

spots.name: Gracie's
spots.summary: Stylish two-story gastropub popular with the younger crowd. Has a patio on each floor and beautiful views of both downtown and the mountains. Live music most nights, not just on weekends. Must be 21 or older.

spots.name: Red Rock Brewing Company

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Downtown brewpub popular for their seafood dishes from Almond Crusted Trout to simple fish and chips. More focus on the food than you might expect from a place that calls itself a brewery.

spots.name: The Locker Room

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Sugar House sports bar that takes on a laid-back bar & grill atmosphere between games. Standard American food: burgers, pizza, etc. Brands itself as very LGBTQ+ friendly.

spots.name: Beer Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This is a biergarten type place that opens at noon and is quiet during the day. They have Kombucha if you don't want to drink beer. Also brats and fries. Good wifi.

spots.name: Bambara
spots.summary: Upscale dining in the New American style, with eclectic décor and top-notch service. Has gluten-free menus for lunch and dinner hours.

spots.name: Hires Big H

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This casual business with a retro vibe has been serving popular burgers and shakes since 1959. It still offers carhop service.

spots.name: Under Current

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An upscale bar serving high quality cocktails as well as a small food menu with items from the seafood restaurant nextdoor.

spots.name: Cafe Trio
spots.summary: Pizza, flatbread, paninis, and pastas with cocktails and wine. They can make many items gluten free, including flat bread.

spots.name: Vegan Daddy Meats

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Vegan versions of comfort fare; they make their own faux meats, which they also sell in packages from the premises.

spots.name: Zest Kitchen & Bar

hours.note: Closed Fri

spots.summary: Upscale all-vegan and gluten-free cuisine. Has oil-free and raw options. Also a bar, so customers must be age 21+.

spots.name: Mahider

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Strip-mall outpost offering classic Ethiopian fare (dining) & specialty grocery items in a laid-back setting.

spots.name: Hong Kong Tea House and Restaurant

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Serves excellent Chinese food. Instead of ordering individual meals, the entire party orders appetizers.

spots.name: Shwe Letyar Sushi

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Located in the Woodbine Food Hall, this spot offers a menu of Burmese dishes (in addition to the sushi.)

spots.name: Copper Common

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat

spots.summary: Cocktail bar with a full food menu. If this wasn't Utah it could probably be called a restaurant.

spots.name: The Rose Establishment

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: No wifi, so it has a more social feel to it. Service charge is included in all prices.
